row.정의: LoCoMo의 QA를 대화, 암시, 반사실, 복합의 네 가지 1인칭 대화 질의 스타일로 다시 쓴 대화형 기억 벤치마크. 검색 재현율과 자유 형식 응답 품질을 따로 평가하며, 암시 질의에 대한 보조 supportive_memory 주석을 함께 제공
row.대표 과제: 기억 시스템이 사용자 발화에서 관련 기억을 검색하고 이를 응답에 반영하는 과제(검색 재현율, 응답 품질)
row.대표 예시·설명: 사용자가 직접 묻지 않는 상황 발화나 잘못된 전제를 담은 발화를 주면, 과거 대화 기억을 찾아 응답에 활용하는지 평가하는 과제 설명
row.이용 시 유의사항: 데이터 라이선스, 상업적 이용, 수정·파생, 재배포 조건과 lm-eval 지원 여부는 확인하지 못함. 원본 LoCoMo 데이터의 조건도 별도로 확인해야 함. 질의 재작성과 supportive_memory 주석은 LLM으로 생성했고 사람 검증은 스타일별 40문항 표본에 한정됨. 응답 채점에 LLM judge가 필요함.

english_copy.axis: Conversational long-term memory invocation (retrieval and response)
english_copy.definition: A conversational memory benchmark that recasts LoCoMo QA items into four first-person query styles: dialog, implicit, counterfactual, and composed. It scores retrieval recall and free-form response quality separately, and provides auxiliary supportive_memory annotations for implicit queries.
english_copy.task: Memory systems retrieve relevant memories from a user utterance and use them in a response (retrieval recall, response quality).
english_copy.example: Task description: the user gives a situational utterance or one with a false premise instead of a direct question, and the assistant must retrieve and use relevant past conversation memories.

screening.paper_title: When Users Don't Ask: Benchmarking Context-Driven Memory Retrieval in Conversational Agents
screening.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increas- ingly deployed as long-horizon conversational agents, motivating growing interest in mem- ory systems. However, existing benchmarks primarily evaluate memory through QA-style probing rather than in-situ conversational usage. We introduce LOCOMO-CONV, a conversa- tional memory benchmark derived from Lo- CoMo with four query styles: dialog, implicit, counterfactual, and composed. Across five rep- resentative memory systems, we evaluate both retrieval recall and end-to-end response qual- ity. Our experiments show that conversational framing exposes substantial retrieval gaps over- looked by QA benchmarks, especially on im- plicit and composed queries, which multi-facet query rewriting narrows for raw-turn mem- ory but not abstractive memory. We further find that strong retrieval does not fully trans- late into response quality, and that implicit queries exhibit silent grounding, where mem- ory improves contextual grounding without ex- plicitly surfacing the gold fact. These results point to reasoning-based memory elaboration as a promising direction, and we release aux- iliary supportive_memory annotations captur- ing conversationally useful context beyond the original gold evidence.
